title: Region Explorer
description: A schematic tile map of the eight countries of South Asia with the Hindu Kush, Himalaya, Western and Eastern Ghats, the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers, and the surrounding seas. Learners click countries to see capitals, 2025 populations (World Bank) and main languages, and animate the southwest monsoon on its normal schedule from late May to about 8 July.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Geography
South Asia
Monsoon
Mountains and rivers
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Locate the eight countries of South Asia on a schematic map.
Explain how the Himalaya, the Hindu Kush and the Ghats shape the region.
Explain how the southwest monsoon spreads across the region and why some areas, such as most of Afghanistan, stay dry.
prerequisites: Basic map reading (north, south, east, west)
Knowing that a country and a region are different things
keyQuestions: Which eight countries make up South Asia?
Where does the southwest monsoon arrive first, and where does it barely reach?
Why do so many people live on the river plains below the Himalaya?
misconceptions: South Asia is the same thing as India.
The Himalaya lies in a single country.
Monsoon means it rains all day, every day.
All of South Asia is hot all year.
controls: Show mountains, rivers and seas checkbox
Click or tap a country tile
dataSources: India Meteorological Department, Monsoon FAQ (normal onset over Kerala around 1 June; covers the country around 8 July): https://mausam.imd.gov.in/imd_latest/monsoonfaq.pdf
